title: Deep Representations for Time-varying Brain Datasets

problem.claim: Representing dynamic brain activities is important for downstream applications, but temporally averaged fMRI provides only a narrow view of those activities.

gap.claim: Previous work lacks the ability to learn and interpret latent dynamics in brain architectures.

contributions.claim: An efficient graph neural network integrates region-mapped fMRI sequences with structural connectivities from DWI.
The approach learns sample-level adaptive adjacency matrices and applies multi-resolution inner cluster smoothing to represent latent brain dynamics.
Integrated gradients are used to identify task-related brain connections and subnetworks, temporal keyframes, and subnetworks discriminating between individual subjects.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe multi-resolution inner cluster smoothing as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report good representations of latent brain dynamics.
The authors report that extensive experiments and ablation studies demonstrate superiority and efficiency in spatial-temporal graph signal modeling.
The authors report that the method provides interpretations of brain dynamics.

narrative_sequence.summary: Dynamic brain activity requires appropriate representations, while temporal averaging limits the available view.
Existing work does not adequately learn or interpret latent brain dynamics.
The paper proposes a graph neural network using fMRI sequences and DWI structural connectivities, with adaptive adjacency learning and multi-resolution smoothing.
Integrated gradients identify important connections, subnetworks, temporal keyframes, and subject-discriminating subnetworks.
Experiments and ablations are reported to show superiority, efficiency, and interpretive insight.
